# Checks

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_check_docs.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every check the audit runs, grouped by rung. 49 checks in total.

- **Required** checks decide the rung. A rung counts only when every required check on it and on every rung below passes.
- **Recommended** checks are reported and never block a rung.
- A check that could not be measured (for example, one that needs `--run`) blocks a rung the same way a failing one does.

For one check in the terminal: `python3 skills/harness-factory/scripts/hf_audit.py --explain <ID>`

## Rung 1: Legible

The agent can find its way and knows the real commands. 9 required, 4 recommended.

### `L1.agent_doc`

**A file that tells the agent how to build and test (agent instructions file: AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without it, the agent guesses how your project works and often guesses wrong. |
| How it is detected | Looks for AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md at the repo root. |
| Fix | Create AGENTS.md at the repo root with your setup, build and test commands, and a CLAUDE.md containing the line @AGENTS.md (the advance skill does both) |

### `L1.agent_doc_wired`

**The agent actually reads AGENTS.md (CLAUDE.md imports it with @AGENTS.md)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Claude Code skips AGENTS.md when a CLAUDE.md exists, so your instructions are silently ignored. |
| How it is detected | If AGENTS.md exists, checks that CLAUDE.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md has an @AGENTS.md import outside code blocks. Evaluated once per agent in config `agents`. |
| Fix | Add the line @AGENTS.md to CLAUDE.md |

### `L1.agent_doc_size`

**Instruction files the agent loads every time are short (200 lines or fewer each)** (recommended)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Long instruction files use up the agent's attention, and it starts missing the rules that matter. |
| How it is detected | Counts lines in CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md. |
| Fix | Shorten CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md to under 200 lines by moving detail into files under docs/ that they link to |

### `L1.commands_documented`

**The instructions file names the real test command** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without a written test command, the agent may skip testing or run the wrong thing. |
| How it is detected | Searches code spans and code blocks in the agent docs (and files they import) for a test command, matching config commands.test, the detected test command or a known test runner. |
| Fix | Add a Commands section to AGENTS.md with the exact test command in backticks, for example `npm test` |

### `L1.refs_resolve`

**Files and commands named in the instructions file really exist** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | When the instructions point at files or commands that are gone, the agent loses trust in them or follows them into errors. |
| How it is detected | Checks paths in backticks and links, `make X`, `just X` and `npm run X` style commands in the agent docs against the files, Makefile targets, justfile recipes and package.json scripts. |
| Fix | Edit AGENTS.md to fix or delete each stale path, make target or package script listed in evidence |

### `L1.test_cmd`

**There is one command that runs the tests** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | If the agent cannot find how to run tests, it cannot check its own work. |
| How it is detected | Uses commands.test from .harness/config.json, else the guess from package.json scripts, Makefile/justfile targets, pyproject, go.mod, Cargo.toml, Gemfile, pom.xml/Gradle or composer.json. |
| Fix | Add a test entry point (a "test" script in package.json or a `test:` target in the Makefile) and set commands.test in .harness/config.json |

### `L1.manifest_lockfile`

**Dependency versions are locked (a lockfile is committed)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without a lockfile, the agent's machine can install different versions than yours and tests fail for reasons nobody can see. |
| How it is detected | For each detected ecosystem, looks for its lockfile (package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, bun.lock, uv.lock, poetry.lock, Cargo.lock, go.sum, Gemfile.lock, composer.lock) or pinned requirements*.txt. |
| Fix | Run your package manager's install (for example `npm install`, `uv lock`, `cargo generate-lockfile`) and commit the lockfile it writes |

### `L1.setup_headless`

**Setup runs without a person typing answers or logging in (best guess)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | An agent running alone cannot answer a prompt or click a login page, so setup just hangs. |
| How it is detected | Scans README, CONTRIBUTING, setup docs and setup/bootstrap/install scripts for prompts (read -p, select), interactive logins (gh auth login, npm login and similar) and click-through phrases. |
| Fix | Change the setup script or README step named in evidence to read values from environment variables or flags instead of prompting |

### `L1.env_example_parity`

**Every environment variable the code reads is listed in .env.example** (recommended)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | The agent cannot run the app if it does not know which settings it needs. |
| How it is detected | Finds env reads in source code (os.getenv, process.env, ENV[], os.Getenv, env::var and similar, tests and harness/CI/agent config dirs excluded) and compares the names with .env.example. |
| Fix | Add each missing variable name with a safe placeholder value to .env.example |

### `L1.git_history`

**The project is in git and has commits** (recommended)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without history the agent cannot see why code changed, and you cannot easily undo its changes. |
| How it is detected | Runs `git rev-list --count HEAD` (read-only). |
| Fix | Run `git init`, then `git add -A && git commit -m "initial commit"` |

### `L1.no_secrets`

**No passwords or API keys are committed** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Anything committed is readable by the agent and everyone with access, and it stays in history after you delete it. |
| How it is detected | Regex scan of tracked and new files for high-confidence key formats (AWS, GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Google, Stripe, Anthropic, OpenAI, npm, private keys), tracked .env files and tracked .claude/settings.local.json. Evidence shows only file:line and the rule name. |
| Fix | Rotate the leaked key first, then delete it from the file and from git history (git filter-repo), and add gitleaks |

### `L1.gitignore`

**Git ignores secrets, per-user settings and build output (.gitignore)** (recommended)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without these entries the agent can commit secrets, personal settings or huge build folders by accident. |
| How it is detected | Asks git whether probe paths (.env, node_modules/, __pycache__/, .venv/, target/, vendor/, .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored by the repo's own ignore files; falls back to reading .gitignore. |
| Fix | Add the entries listed in evidence to .gitignore |

### `L1.harness_config`

**The harness settings file .harness/config.json exists and is valid** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Every later step reads its commands and branch name from this file, so nothing else can be set up without it. |
| How it is detected | Parses .harness/config.json and checks the schema: schema 1, default_branch, commands.*, core_flow, protected_paths, human_only_areas, max_diff_lines, maintainers, optional agents. |
| Fix | Run the advance skill, which asks you a few questions and writes .harness/config.json |

## Rung 2: Verifiable

"Done" can be proven by a command. 9 required, 3 recommended.

### `V2.tests_exist`

**The project has automated tests** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | With no tests, a passing test run proves nothing and the agent's changes go unchecked. |
| How it is detected | Counts files that match common test naming (test_*.py, *_test.go, *.test.ts, *_spec.rb, *Test.java, files under tests/ or __tests__/), and Rust files with #[test]. |
| Fix | Add at least one test file (for example tests/test_smoke.py or src/app.test.ts) that runs with your test command |

### `V2.gates_script`

**One script decides pass or fail (.harness/bin/gates.sh with at least one real gate)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without one command that says pass or fail, the agent decides for itself whether its work is done. |
| How it is detected | Checks .harness/bin/gates.sh exists, is committed as executable, has no HARNESS_STUB marker and matches the shipped script rendered with .harness/config.json (unless listed in config customized_scripts); and that .harness/gates.conf has at least one required gate that is not a stub. |
| Fix | Run the advance skill for rung 2 to install .harness/bin/gates.sh, then list a real required gate (your test command) in .harness/gates.conf |

### `V2.gates_pass`

**The gates pass right now (needs --run)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | If the gates already fail before the agent starts, it cannot tell its own mistakes from old ones. |
| How it is detected | Only with --run: executes .harness/bin/gates.sh with a timeout; exit 0 is pass. Without --run it is not_measured. |
| Fix | Run `.harness/bin/gates.sh`, fix what fails, then re-run the audit with --run |

### `V2.smoke_defined`

**A quick check that the main feature still works (.harness/bin/smoke.sh is filled in)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Tests can pass while the app itself is broken; a smoke check catches that. |
| How it is detected | Checks .harness/bin/smoke.sh exists, is executable and no longer contains the HARNESS_STUB marker. |
| Fix | Edit .harness/bin/smoke.sh: replace the stub with a command that exercises your core flow, and remove the HARNESS_STUB marker |

### `V2.smoke_pass`

**The smoke check passes right now (needs --run)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | A smoke check that already fails cannot warn anyone when the agent breaks something. |
| How it is detected | Only with --run: executes .harness/bin/smoke.sh with a timeout; exit 0 is pass. Without --run it is not_measured. |
| Fix | Run `.harness/bin/smoke.sh`, fix what fails, then re-run the audit with --run |

### `V2.evidence_rules`

**Rules that tell the agent to show proof (test output) before saying it is done** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without these rules the agent may say "done" without showing that anything was tested. |
| How it is detected | Checks the agent-neutral .harness/docs/evidence.md exists and is not empty; reports whether the Claude copy .claude/rules/evidence.md is present when claude is a configured agent. |
| Fix | Run the advance skill for rung 2 to install .harness/docs/evidence.md (and .claude/rules/evidence.md for Claude) |

### `V2.stop_hook_effective`

**The agent is stopped from finishing until it has proof (a Stop hook that really runs)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Written rules can be ignored; a hook is checked by the tool itself every time the agent tries to stop. |
| How it is detected | Reads the committed .claude/settings.json, finds Stop command hooks, and checks the script each one runs exists inside the repo (and is executable when run directly). Evaluated once per agent in config `agents`. |
| Fix | Run the advance skill for rung 2; it registers the Stop hook in .claude/settings.json and installs its script under .harness/hooks/ |

### `V2.verify_skill`

**The agent has a written procedure for checking its work (verify skill)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without a fixed checking procedure, each run of the agent checks its work differently, or not at all. |
| How it is detected | For Claude: checks .claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md exists and is not empty. Evaluated once per agent in config `agents`. |
| Fix | Run the advance skill for rung 2 to install .claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md |

### `V2.pr_template_evidence`

**The pull request form asks for evidence** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Reviewers then have to trust the agent's word instead of seeing proof. |
| How it is detected | Looks for a PR template (.github/pull_request_template.md and the other GitHub locations) with a heading or bold label containing "Evidence". |
| Fix | Add an "## Evidence" section to .github/pull_request_template.md asking for the test and smoke output |

### `V2.lint_configured`

**A linter (automatic style and mistake checker) is set up** (recommended)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | A linter catches many small mistakes before a human has to. |
| How it is detected | Looks for common linter config files, [tool.ruff]/[tool.pylint] in pyproject.toml, eslintConfig in package.json, or a detected lint command. |
| Fix | Add a linter config for your language (for example ruff.toml, eslint.config.js or .golangci.yml) and a lint command |

### `V2.types_configured`

**A type checker is set up (or the language checks types itself)** (recommended)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Type checks catch wrong arguments and missing fields that tests often miss. |
| How it is detected | Looks for tsconfig.json, mypy/pyright config, PHPStan/Psalm, Sorbet/Steep, or a statically typed language (Go, Rust, Java, Kotlin). |
| Fix | Add a type checker config (for example tsconfig.json with "strict": true, or mypy.ini) |

### `V2.ci_runs_gates`

**CI runs the same gates on every pull request** (recommended)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | If CI does not run the same gates, a change that fails them can still be merged. |
| How it is detected | Searches .github/workflows/*.yml (comments ignored, agent workflows skipped) for a line that runs .harness/bin/gates.sh. Fails if that job is disabled, sets continue-on-error, or ignores the result (\|\| true). |
| Fix | Add a step `run: .harness/bin/gates.sh` to a workflow in .github/workflows/ that runs on pull_request |

## Rung 3: Guarded

Mistakes stay small and visible. 9 required, 3 recommended.

### `G3.protected_paths`

**A list of files the agent must never change (.harness/protected-paths.txt)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without this list, the agent can edit the tests or checks that are supposed to judge it. |
| How it is detected | Checks .harness/protected-paths.txt has at least one line that is not blank or a comment. |
| Fix | Create .harness/protected-paths.txt with one path or glob per line (start with .harness/ and .github/workflows/) |

### `G3.diff_guard`

**A script that rejects changes to protected files or changes that are too big (.harness/bin/diff-guard.sh)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without it, a change that rewrites protected files or thousands of lines looks like any other change. |
| How it is detected | Checks .harness/bin/diff-guard.sh exists, is committed as executable, has no HARNESS_STUB marker, and that it and .harness/bin/harness_guard.py (which it runs) match the shipped scripts rendered with .harness/config.json, unless listed in config customized_scripts. |
| Fix | Run the advance skill for rung 3 to install .harness/bin/diff-guard.sh |

### `G3.pretool_guard_effective`

**A guard runs before every agent action: protected paths need a human's approval, forbidden actions are blocked, a crash blocks** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without a guard that fails closed, a crash or timeout quietly lets the forbidden action through. |
| How it is detected | For Claude: reads .claude/settings.json (and fails if it or .claude/settings.local.json sets disableAllHooks) and needs a PreToolUse command hook with "onFailure": "block" whose script exists in the repo (and is executable when run directly) and matches the shipped script rendered with .harness/config.json (unless listed in config customized_scripts). onFailure requires Claude Code v2.1.295 or later; older versions ignore it and let the action through when the hook fails. The shipped guard answers "ask" for protected paths and exits 2 for .harness/acceptance/. Evaluated once per agent in config `agents`. |
| Fix | Run the advance skill for rung 3; it registers a PreToolUse hook with "onFailure": "block" in .claude/settings.json |

### `G3.deny_rules`

**The agent is forbidden to merge pull requests or push to the main branch, and harness edits need approval** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without these rules, nothing stops the agent from shipping its own change without review. |
| How it is detected | For Claude: tests permissions.deny in .claude/settings.json against sample commands `gh pr merge 1` and `git push origin <default branch>` using Claude Code's rule matching, and needs an ask or deny Edit rule naming .harness and AGENTS.md (ask rules prompt in every permission mode and are denied when no one can answer). Evaluated once per agent in config `agents`. |
| Fix | Add "Bash(gh pr merge *)" and "Bash(git push * <default branch>*)" style rules to permissions.deny and "Edit(/.harness/**)", "Edit(AGENTS.md)" to permissions.ask (or deny) in .claude/settings.json (the rung 3 template does this) |

### `G3.acceptance_protected`

**The acceptance tests are locked against agent edits (.harness/acceptance/)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | If the agent can edit the tests that judge it, it can make them pass without doing the work. |
| How it is detected | Checks .harness/protected-paths.txt lists .harness/acceptance and, for each configured agent, that its deny rules cover edits there (Claude: an Edit/Write deny rule naming .harness/acceptance; an ask rule does not count, since a person at the prompt could approve it). |
| Fix | Add .harness/acceptance/ to .harness/protected-paths.txt and "Edit(/.harness/acceptance/**)" to permissions.deny in .claude/settings.json |

### `G3.ci_guard`

**CI runs the gates, the diff guard and the workflow checker on every pull request** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Local guards can be skipped; CI is the place every change has to pass through. |
| How it is detected | Looks for one workflow that triggers on pull_request and references gates.sh, diff-guard.sh and lint-agent-workflows.py. Fails if that job is disabled (if: false), sets continue-on-error, or ignores a script's result (\|\| true). |
| Fix | Run the advance skill for rung 3 to install the guard workflow in .github/workflows/ (it runs gates.sh, diff-guard.sh and lint-agent-workflows.py) |

### `G3.ci_runs_gates`

**CI runs the same gates on every pull request** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | If CI does not run the same gates, a change that fails them can still be merged. |
| How it is detected | Searches .github/workflows/*.yml (comments ignored, agent workflows skipped) for a line that runs .harness/bin/gates.sh. Fails if that job is disabled, sets continue-on-error, or ignores the result (\|\| true). |
| Fix | Add a step `run: .harness/bin/gates.sh` to a workflow in .github/workflows/ that runs on pull_request |

### `G3.workflow_lint_clean`

**The agent workflows pass the safety checker (needs --run)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | An unsafe workflow can let text from a stranger's issue control the agent or leak secrets. |
| How it is detected | Only with --run: executes .harness/bin/lint-agent-workflows.py with python3; exit 0 is pass. Without --run it is not_measured. |
| Fix | Run `python3 .harness/bin/lint-agent-workflows.py`, fix each finding in .github/workflows/, then re-run the audit with --run |

### `G3.branch_protection`

**GitHub blocks direct pushes to the main branch (branch protection)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Repo settings files can be changed by the agent; GitHub's own protection is the lock it cannot pick. |
| How it is detected | Makes the audit's only network call: `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/branches/BRANCH` and reads `protected`. Unknown when --offline, gh is missing or not logged in, or there is no GitHub remote. |
| Fix | On GitHub open Settings > Branches (or Rules) and protect the default branch: require a pull request and the gates check |

### `G3.codeowners`

**Named owners must review changes to sensitive files (CODEOWNERS)** (recommended)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without owners, a change to the harness itself can be approved by anyone. |
| How it is detected | Looks for a non-empty CODEOWNERS in the repo root, .github/ or docs/. |
| Fix | Create .github/CODEOWNERS with lines like `.harness/ @your-team` and `.github/ @your-team` |

### `G3.secret_scanning`

**A secret scanner runs automatically (gitleaks or similar)** (recommended)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | The basic scan here only knows a few key formats; a real scanner catches far more before they are pushed. |
| How it is detected | Looks for .gitleaks.toml, or gitleaks, trufflehog or detect-secrets in .pre-commit-config.yaml or any workflow. |
| Fix | Add a gitleaks step to CI or to .pre-commit-config.yaml, for example the gitleaks/gitleaks-action workflow step |

### `G3.sandbox_settings`

**Agent commands run in a sandbox that refuses to run unsandboxed** (recommended)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without a sandbox, one bad command from the agent can touch anything on the machine. |
| How it is detected | For Claude: checks .claude/settings.json has sandbox.enabled true and sandbox.failIfUnavailable true (otherwise it silently runs unsandboxed where the sandbox is unsupported). Evaluated once per agent in config `agents`. |
| Fix | Set "sandbox": {"enabled": true, "failIfUnavailable": true} in .claude/settings.json |

## Rung 4: First loop

One unattended automation that can only comment or label. 6 required, 0 recommended.

### `F4.agent_workflow`

**At least one CI workflow runs the agent** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | This rung is about letting the agent work from CI; without a workflow there is no loop to run. |
| How it is detected | Looks in .github/workflows/ for a workflow that uses anthropics/claude-code-action or calls the claude CLI (comment lines ignored). |
| Fix | Run the advance skill for rung 4 to install the first agent workflow in .github/workflows/ |

### `F4.kill_switch`

**Every agent workflow can be switched off with one setting (AGENT_ENABLED)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | When the agent misbehaves you need to stop it in one click, not by editing every workflow. |
| How it is detected | For each job in an agent workflow that invokes the agent, checks the job-level `if:` mentions vars.AGENT_ENABLED (comments ignored; a mention elsewhere, such as an env value or a step, does not count). |
| Fix | Add `if: vars.AGENT_ENABLED == 'true'` to each agent job and create the repo variable AGENT_ENABLED under Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions |

### `F4.maintainers`

**A list of people allowed to start the agent (.harness/maintainers.txt)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without it, anyone who can open an issue might be able to set the agent to work. |
| How it is detected | Checks .harness/maintainers.txt has at least one line that is not blank or a comment. |
| Fix | Create .harness/maintainers.txt with one GitHub username per line |

### `F4.attribution`

**Agent pull requests are labelled agent:* and carry an Agent-Run: line** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without a label you cannot tell agent work from human work, so you cannot measure whether the agent helps. |
| How it is detected | Looks in the PR templates, agent workflows and .harness/bin/agent-output.py (which writes the Agent-Run: line on every comment the shipped loops post) for an agent: label pattern and the text Agent-Run:. |
| Fix | Make the agent workflow add an `agent:<name>` label and an `Agent-Run: <run id>` line to each PR it opens (the rung 4 template does this) |

### `F4.budget_caps`

**Every agent job has a time limit and a turn limit** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without limits a stuck agent can run for hours and spend a lot of money. |
| How it is detected | For each job in an agent workflow that invokes the agent, looks for timeout-minutes: and --max-turns in that job. |
| Fix | Add `timeout-minutes: 30` to each agent job and `--max-turns 30` to its claude_args |

### `F4.ledger`

**A log of audits and installs exists (.harness/ledger.jsonl)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without a log you cannot see how the harness changed over time or what it was when something broke. |
| How it is detected | Checks .harness/ledger.jsonl exists. |
| Fix | Run `python3 scripts/hf_audit.py --repo . --append-ledger` from the plugin, or the advance skill, to start .harness/ledger.jsonl |

## Rung 5: Factory

Issue to draft pull request, measured. 5 required, 1 recommended.

### `X5.implement_lane`

**An agent workflow that writes code, started only by a listed maintainer** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Letting anyone trigger code-writing agents lets strangers spend your budget and steer your code. |
| How it is detected | Looks for an agent workflow triggered by `labeled` or `workflow_dispatch` that references .harness/maintainers.txt. |
| Fix | Run the advance skill for rung 5 to install the implement workflow; it starts on a label or manual run and checks .harness/maintainers.txt |

### `X5.monitor`

**A scheduled job watches the agents' results** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without someone or something looking regularly, a broken agent keeps opening bad pull requests unnoticed. |
| How it is detected | Looks for a workflow with a schedule (cron) that runs the agent or a .harness/bin/ script. |
| Fix | Run the advance skill for rung 5 to install the scheduled monitor workflow in .github/workflows/ |

### `X5.metrics_script`

**A script that measures how well the agents do (.harness/bin/metrics.*)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without numbers you cannot tell whether the agents save time or create more work. |
| How it is detected | Looks for .harness/bin/metrics.py, metrics.sh or another .harness/bin/metrics* file without the HARNESS_STUB marker. |
| Fix | Run the advance skill for rung 5 to install .harness/bin/metrics.py |

### `X5.failure_library`

**Past agent failures are written down as cases (.harness/failures/)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | If failures are not recorded, the same mistakes come back and nobody notices the pattern. |
| How it is detected | Counts files in .harness/failures/ other than README and .gitkeep; at least 1 passes, 20 or more is the goal. |
| Fix | Add one file per agent failure to .harness/failures/ (what happened, how it was caught, the rule that prevents it); aim for 20 |

### `X5.rules_inbox`

**A place where repeated mistakes become proposed rules (.harness/rules-inbox.md)** (required)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | Without it, lessons from failures stay in people's heads instead of becoming checks. |
| How it is detected | Checks .harness/rules-inbox.md or a .harness/rules-inbox/ directory exists. |
| Fix | Create .harness/rules-inbox.md (the rung 5 template does) and let the monitor add rule candidates there |

### `X5.holdout`

**Some acceptance scenarios are hidden from the agent (holdout)** (recommended)

| | |
|---|---|
| Why it matters | An agent that can read every test can learn to pass the tests instead of solving the problem. |
| How it is detected | Per .harness/docs/factory.md the holdout lives outside the repo, so a static audit cannot see it. Fails when a holdout directory sits in the repo (agent-readable), passes when a workflow references a holdout (the eval job), otherwise unknown. |
| Fix | Keep holdout tasks outside the agent-readable tree (a separate private repository or an encrypted CI artifact) and read them only from an eval job, as .harness/docs/factory.md describes |
